title: Console rollouts: toast focus management, SR announcements, and language-switch flow
creator: Ava Morales
description: Design and prototype accessibility- and localization-focused behaviors for rollout toasts and ephemeral UI in the Redwood Console. This ticket covers: 1) keyboard focus behavior when toasts appear (avoid focus loss and preserve tab order), 2) ARIA announcements and polite/assertive selection rules for different toast severity levels, 3) color contrast tokens and a high-contrast mode variant for rollout and cost-related toasts, and 4) language switch flow ensuring the console preserves user context, announces language changes, and correctly formats localized numbers in active alerts. Work spans design spec, interactive prototype, and guidance for engineering on implementation patterns and regression tests.
acceptance_criteria: When a non-modal toast appears it must not forcibly steal focus from a keyboard user; explicit focusable actions inside a toast are reachable by keyboard and are in the tab order.
Critical toasts (errors or rollbacks) use aria-live='assertive' and are announced to screen readers; informational toasts use aria-live='polite'.
All toast backgrounds, text, and action buttons meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) in default theme and 7:1 in high-contrast mode.
Language switch from header preserves user context (same route, same open panel) and triggers an unobtrusive SR announcement: 'Interface language changed to <language>'.
Locale-aware number formatting is applied for active cost/usage values inside toasts immediately after language switch (no visual flicker or truncated layout).
Interactive prototype demonstrates keyboard traversal and SR announcements for at least three toast variants: info, success, error (rollback).
Engineering has an implementation proposal (PR) linked and an initial e2e a11y test case covering focus andannounce behavior.
Accessibility review signoff from Kate Rivera (a11y reviewer) is present in comments.
design_notes: Prioritized non-invasive behavior for keyboard and screen-reader users: do not trap focus for ephemeral toasts. For toasts that include critical actions (e.g., 'Rollback now'), provide an explicit keyboard-focusable control and ensure that the tab order respects the page sequence. Use aria-describedby for visual context (link to rollout name) and aria-live regions placed at app root to avoid duplication. For i18n, avoid embedding language-specific punctuation in SR messages; use localized templates. Implement color tokens that map to existing theme tokens and a high-contrast overlay style for users that opt into it.
decisions: Use aria-live regions at the application root rather than inside individual toast elements to centralize announcements (minimizes duplicate announcements in nested toasts).
Default to aria-live='polite' for non-blocking toasts; switch to 'assertive' only for rollback/fatal errors to avoid SR spam.
Do not auto-shift keyboard focus onto transient toasts. Focus moves only when user activates a toast action.
Use Intl.NumberFormat with user's selected locale for formatting costs inside toasts; engineering to provide fallback for older browsers.
High-contrast mode uses a single contrast token set mapped in tokens/color-contrast-rollouts so it can be toggled at the theme level.
tradeoffs: We chose not to auto-focus critical toasts to avoid context loss, which means keyboard users must actively tab to rollback actions. This increases discoverability burden but reduces interruptive behavior and accidental destructive actions. Using centralized aria-live reduces duplication but requires slight refactor in the toast system (root-level announcement queue). Implementing perfect locale number formatting in all browsers may require polyfills for older environments — engineering accepted the polyfill cost for correctness.
